title: The ALMA-ATOMS-QUARKS Survey: Resolving a Chemically Rich Massive Protostellar Outflow
question: What are the physical and chemical structures and the chemical origins of molecular species within the bipolar protostellar outflow of the high-mass star-forming region SDC335?

data.angular_resolution: Band 3 12-m continuum: 1.7'' x 1.5''; Band 6 TM2+ACA: ~1.3'' x 1.1''; Band 6 ACA+TM1+TM2: 0.34'' (best 0.3'')
data.sensitivity: 3 mm continuum rms: 10 mJy beam^-1; 1.3 mm continuum rms: ~0.8 mJy beam^-1

what.value: Total gas mass of the SDC335 clump (~3700 M_sun)

evidence.quote: This clump contains a total gas mass of ∼3700 M⊙ (C. J. Cyganowski et al. 2008; M. Anderson et al. 2021).

external_data.citation: C. J. Cyganowski et al. 2008; M. Anderson et al. 2021

what.value: Mass of the central region encompassing massive core SDC335-C1 (~400 M_sun)

evidence.quote: Within the central region corresponding to the area shown in Figure 1 (b), which encompasses the massive core SDC335-C1, the mass is ∼400 M⊙ (F. Xu et al. 2023)

what.value: Detection of 18 COMs toward C1 in the ATOMS 3mm survey

evidence.quote: In the ATOMS 3mm band survey, 18 COMs were detected toward C1, including c-C2H4O, C2H5CN, CH3CHO, and CH3OCHO (S.-L. Qin et al. 2022; Z.-Y. Li et al. 2025), indicating that it is a typical hot molecular core.

external_data.citation: S.-L. Qin et al. 2022; Z.-Y. Li et al. 2025

recipe.goal: Extract line spectra at knots and identify molecular transitions
recipe.method: Extract 3 mm and 1.3 mm spectra at the seven bright knots along the walls of the jet-driven outflow cavity and identify transitions

recipe.goal: Construct velocity channel maps, integrated intensity (moment 0) maps, and position-velocity diagrams (PVDs)
recipe.method: Integrate ACA+TM1+TM2 data over 3 km s^-1 channels for channel maps; integrate blue-shifted, systemic, and red-shifted velocity components for moment 0 maps; extract PVDs along the outflow-jet axis (K1-K7)
key_parameters: Channel map velocity bin: 3 km s^-1 (±1.3 km s^-1 around each velocity)
CO (2-1) RGB velocity intervals: -42 to -12 km s^-1 (blue), ±12 km s^-1 (green), +12 to +42 km s^-1 (red)

recipe.goal: Calculate position-integrated intensities and relative abundance ratios along the jet axis
recipe.method: Compute integrated intensities along the outflow axis with a 1'' slit width over -36 to +36 km s^-1, normalize to reference value at 2'' from C1, and divide by local 13CO intensity as a proxy for relative abundance
key_parameters: Slit width = 1'', velocity range = -36 to +36 km s^-1, inner hot-core exclusion radius = 2''
assumptions: LTE and optically thin conditions; 13CO traces H2 column density

recipe.goal: Derive gas rotational/kinetic temperature along the outflow axis from H2CO transitions
recipe.method: Model H2CO 3-2 line ratios along the outflow axis using non-LTE radiative transfer code RADEX and compare with the spatial derivative of SiO/13CO intensity ratio

recipe.goal: Classify molecular species using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and pairwise Kendall rank correlations
recipe.method: Perform PCA on the molecular PVDs along the jet axis (excluding inner ±2'') and compute pairwise Kendall rank correlation coefficients between integrated intensities of molecular lines
key_parameters: PCA input dimensions: 18,684-dimensional vectors (173 positions x 108 high-velocity channels), inner ±2'' of C1 excluded

answer_key.quantity: Maximum line-of-sight velocity of the bipolar jet

evidence.quote: Consistently, the PVD (Fig.3) and moment0 map (Fig.2) show that the bipolar jet driven by C1 is remarkably symmetric within ±14′′ in both morphology and velocity, reaching line-of-sight velocities of up to ±40 km s−1 at ∼±10′′ from C1.

answer_key.quantity: Maximum line width at knots K1, K6, and K7

evidence.quote: The broadest line widths (up to 20 km s−1) and the highest gas temperatures are found at knots K1, K6, and K7, coinciding with peaks in molecular emission.

answer_key.quantity: H2CO rotational temperature at several knots

evidence.quote: Independent constraints from H2CO rotational analysis (Fig. B4) reveal Trot ≳ 200 K at several knots, consistent with strong shock heating by the protostellar jet

answer_key.quantity: Kendall correlation coefficient between SiO J=2-1 and J=5-4

evidence.quote: Complementing this, pairwise Kendall correlations (Fig. 5) reveal that CS, SO, HCN, and SiO are tightly correlated (> 0.8), with the strongest correlation (0.88) between two SiO transitions J=2–1 and J=5–4.

answer_key.quantity: Kendall correlation coefficient between H2CO and HCO+

evidence.quote: H2CO and HCO+ correlate uniformly with most species (0.77–0.83) and with each other (0.86), indicating strong chemical coupling.

answer_key.quantity: Kendall correlation coefficient between CH3OH 2_-1,1-1_-1,0 A and 4_-2,3-3_-1,2 E

evidence.quote: Notably, CH3OH 2−1,1–1−1,0 A and 4−2,3–3−1,2 E correlate at only 0.79, and their correlations with other molecules show larger differences, possibly related to nuclear spin isomers (Zou et al., in prep).
